why_trail.why: Handoff is complete on all seven fields. Two defects confirmed at the anchor: literal <branch> and OPEN-only. Third property confirmed in code, not just prose -- checklist_engine._run_check_command runs [bash,-c,command] and _check_condition takes returncode only, so --jq 'length > 0' can never carry a verdict. resolve_spine substitutes <repo-root> via Path.resolve().as_posix() and does NOT own <branch>, so instantiation cannot catch it. No jq on PATH: the stub gh must model the --jq itself, deriving its behaviour FROM the expression text so the expression stays load-bearing.

archive.c2b rewritten to the pre-ruled shape; the four-state matrix collects 4 tests / 4 subtests and exits 0. The RED run recorded a fact the handoff did not predict: the shipped unquoted <branch> is a SHELL REDIRECTION, so the old check failed for OPEN and MERGED too and only 'passed' the two states it was supposed to reject -- it was an always-fails check, not just an OPEN-only one. Stub gh derives its filtering FROM the --jq text, so the selector stays load-bearing.

archive_mutation collects 2 tests / 9 subtests, exit 0. The disagreement assertion is the anti-no-op mechanism the g2 review asked for: a leg that agreed with the real check on its own fixture would fail even if its own directional assertion passed. The exit-code leg is DERIVED from the shipped text by unwrapping the shell comparison, not retyped, so it cannot drift away from what ships.
